paper_metadata.title: Significantly Improving the High-Temperature Tensile Properties of Al17Cr10Fe36Ni36Mo1 Alloys by Microalloying Hf

attributes.size: width 1~5 nm for acicular phase; length <50 nm for needle-shaped phase
attributes.morphology: acicular/needle-shaped at grain and phase boundaries and inside B2
attributes.location: grain boundaries, phase boundaries, B2 phase

evidence.quote: In Al17Cr10Fe35.5Ni36Mo1Hf0.5 alloys, precipitation of the Hf-rich phase precipitated at grain boundaries and phase boundaries. In addition, the acicular Hf-rich phases with widths of 1~5 nm interlaced with each other and precipitated in the B2 phase were also observed.
With the increase in Hf content, the dual-phase structure with the FCC phase and B2 phase is almost unchanged
the fracture surface of the Hf0.5 alloys was ﬁlled by dimples, which revealed the ductile transgranular fracture mode
numerous narrow and long microcracks located in the FCC phase can be found, and there are a few phase boundary microcracks
the Hf-rich phases at grain and phase boundaries in the Hf0.5 alloys would pin grain and phase boundaries to hinder their sliding during high-temperature deformation
the needle-shaped Hf-rich phase with a length of less than 50 nm distributed in the B2 phase (Figure 3a) hindered the movement of dislocations at high temperatures
stress concentration near the grain boundary microcracks was observed, which was related to thermally activated grain boundary sliding and the accumulation of dislocations in their vicinity
obvious grain facets (orange arrow) and interface cracks (blue arrow) were observed on the fracture surface, as shown in Figure 7a, revealing the brittle intergranular fracture mode
the fracture surface of the Hf0.5 alloys was ﬁlled by dimples, which revealed the ductile transgranular fracture mode
This indicates that the Hf0 alloy had undergone signiﬁcant softening at 700 ◦C, related to the softening of the B2 phase in the alloys at high temperatures [39].
